name: Max Bass
role: Proprietor of the Riverside Hotel, Belfield
bio: Max Bass ran the Riverside Hotel at Belfield, which the Cow Boy's Belfield columns in 1884 praised as one of the best on the Northern Pacific line, noting his plans for an addition and fresh paint. He signed the call for the April 1884 Republican county convention, which elected him to the county central committee, and that October, with George Blankenberg, he signed a notice as a committee member protesting the chairman's conduct; in June 1884 the paper announced his marriage to Miss Martha Geissel of New York. In May 1885 he was reported refusing to pay a $15 license fee demanded of Belfield saloon-keepers, and by July 1885 he had become an agent for the Milwaukee Brewing Co.
